items.title: Privacy egress monitor
items.summary: Live tracking of what certified/legitimate apps actually send — moving CounterSpy from 'is this spyware?' to 'this app is trusted, but here's what it's exfiltrating; do you consent?'. A per-process egress observer (destination/volume tracking, consent deltas). v1 (now in development): a live TUI 'egress top' via sudo-CLI observation (nettop + lsof), observe-only. Rationale: the v0.3.0 feedback loop measures false positives among flagged apps; the next risk surface is the apps NOT flagged — notarized/allowlisted software that over-collects. Rhymes with the egress-only invariant: watch egress because egress is where the risk lives.

items.title: Phase 1 — Passive reveal: destination names + cleartext extraction
items.summary: IN PROGRESS on feat/egress-names (all reviewed): first phase of the outbound-visibility program (see docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-14-outbound-traffic-visibility-design.md). Passive DNS-response capture (port 53) builds an IP->hostname cache so the egress tree/zoom/inspect show the name an app actually resolved instead of a bare cloud IP; and the on-demand inspector gains maximal cleartext extraction (structured HTTP request/response, headers, path, body preview) beyond today's text-or-hexdump. No decryption. Reuses a filter-parameterized /dev/bpf capture shared with the per-flow inspector. Names also feed a light-touch, corroboration-gated raw-IP concern signal (the existing allRawIP bump switched on). Foundation for Phases 2-3.

items.title: TLS key-log decryption (SSLKEYLOGFILE) — optional add-on
items.summary: Optional, non-invasive complement to the proxy: decrypt flows from apps launched with SSLKEYLOGFILE (browsers/curl/Go tooling) using keys they already export. Demoted from a phase to an add-on because it only reaches apps you launch with the env var — blind to Safari/native apps/already-running daemons — so the transparent proxy (now Phase 2) is the real broad-visibility path. Lower priority; layer onto the proxy's capture if wanted.

items.title: Phase 2 — Transparent TLS-intercepting decrypt mirror
items.summary: Pulled forward from Phase 3 (approved in brainstorming, see docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-15-phase2-tls-interception-design.md): a consented, transparent, READ-ONLY intercepting proxy (local root CA + pf rdr redirect of TCP:443, original dest via /dev/pf DIOCNATLOOK, crypto/tls terminate+re-dial+relay). Decrypts already-running apps' HTTPS broadly — the 'visibility into all encrypted traffic' goal — and surfaces the plaintext via DecodeCleartext+Redact. Runs as `counterspy intercept` (background daemon, publishes decrypted flows over a live socket and/or a rotating/expiring log chosen at launch); `counterspy console` is a separate viewer. Honest coverage: pinned apps bypassed-not-broken, QUIC/opaque labeled. No traffic modification this cycle.

items.title: Phase 3 — Active egress controls: redact + block
items.summary: On top of the proven Phase-2 decrypt proxy: strip sensitive fields from outbound payloads and/or block transmissions by rule. This is the phase that crosses the observe-only network invariant into active control (DLP). Sequenced after the read-only decrypt mirror has a track record so a bug can't silently mangle a user's request before interception is trustworthy.

items.title: Sign + notarize the release binaries
items.summary: Add Apple Developer ID codesigning + notarytool notarization to the GoReleaser release pipeline so prebuilt binaries run without any Gatekeeper friction. The v0.4.x release tooling ships UNSIGNED first (curl|sh and Homebrew avoid the quarantine flag; a browser-downloaded tar.gz needs xattr -d com.apple.quarantine); the intent is to wire signing imminently once a Developer ID cert + notarization secrets are in CI. Important for a security tool that runs under sudo — users rightly distrust an unsigned binary. The pipeline is structured so signing is a drop-in step.

items.title: Non-interactive / headless mode with rotating log output
items.summary: A maintainer-approved --non-interactive flag that runs CounterSpy's monitoring WITHOUT the interactive TUI, directing output to either the console (stdout) or a file with log rollover, a size limit, and expiration/retention. Default mode stays interactive (today's `console`). Rationale: many capabilities — the egress monitor, per-flow inspection, destination names, and the planned decryption/proxy phases — are currently gated behind the interactive console TUI; a headless mode is the mechanism to surface them for background/service execution and durable logging. Generalizes the existing one-shot `console --json`/`--once` non-TTY path into a CONTINUOUS logging run, and will likely require lifting some capabilities out of the TUI-gated code path so they can run headlessly. Per the standing 'no new CLI flags without explicit approval' rule, --non-interactive is maintainer-named and pre-approved for its future phase (not for the current Phase-1 traffic work).
